content: 1. Take 35 mg of the medication orally once daily at the same time each day. If a dose is delayed by more than 3 hours, use an additional method of contraception for the next 48 hours. Administration should be continuous without any interruption between pill packs. Begin the first pill pack on the first day of menstruation or the day after a miscarriage or abortion. This medication is not recommended for premenarcheal individuals. 2. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 3. Acitretin decreases the effects of norethindrone through an unknown mechanism. This combination is contraindicated as it may result in contraceptive failure. 4. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Apalutamide, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, can lower the exposure of drugs metabolized by CYP3A4. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for loss of therapeutic effect and adjust the dose as needed. 5. Belzutifan decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Belzutifan may lead to contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding. Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective nonhormonal contraception. Based on animal studies, belzutifan may cause fetal harm. 6. Bosentan decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 7. Brigatinib decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Brigatinib can reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives and may cause fetal harm. Women should use effective nonhormonal contraception during treatment and for at least 4 months after the last dose. 8. Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefit outweighs the risk. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable when coadministered with carbamazepine, and concomitant use may increase menstrual-related adverse effects such as amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, or menorrhagia. 9. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 10. Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefit outweighs the risk. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable when coadministered with enzalutamide, and concomitant use may increase menstrual-related adverse effects. 11. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Fexinidazole may increase the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. 12. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefit outweighs the risk. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable when coadministered with fosphenytoin, and concomitant use may increase menstrual-related adverse effects. 13. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Idelalisib is a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor; avoid coadministration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 14. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for loss of therapeutic effect and adjust the dose as needed. 15. Lesinurad decreases the effects of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Use additional nonhormonal contraception methods, as hormonal contraception alone is not reliable when taking lesinurad. 16. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor response to estrogens and progestins when a CYP3A4 inducer is added or discontinued, and adjust hormone dosage as necessary. Advise additional or alternative nonhormonal birth control during and after coadministration with CYP3A4 inducers. 17. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefit outweighs the risk. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable when coadministered with lumacaftor/ivacaftor, and concomitant use may increase menstrual-related adverse effects. 18. Mavacamten decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Mavacamten may decrease systemic exposures of ethinyl estradiol and progestin, leading to contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding. Advise patients to use a contraceptive method unaffected by CYP450 enzyme induction or add nonhormonal contraception during and for 4 months after the last dose. 19. Mitotane decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefit outweighs the risk. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable when coadministered with mitotane, and concomitant use may increase menstrual-related adverse effects. 20. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefit outweighs the risk. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable when coadministered with phenobarbital, and concomitant use may increase menstrual-related adverse effects. 21. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefit outweighs the risk. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable when coadministered with phenytoin, and concomitant use may increase menstrual-related adverse effects. 22. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefit outweighs the risk. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable when coadministered with primidone, and concomitant use may increase menstrual-related adverse effects. 23. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefit outweighs the risk. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable when coadministered with rifabutin, and concomitant use may increase menstrual-related adverse effects. 24. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefit outweighs the risk. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable when coadministered with rifampin. Use nonhormonal contraception. 25. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefit outweighs the risk. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable when coadministered with rifapentine, and concomitant use may increase menstrual-related adverse effects. 26. Sugammadex sodium decreases the effects of norethindrone by receptor binding competition. A sugammadex bolus dose is equivalent to missing doses of hormonal contraceptives. If an oral contraceptive is taken on the same day as sugammadex, or if the patient uses a transdermal or implant hormonal contraceptive, additional nonhormonal contraception is required for the next 7 days. 27. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 28. Topiramate decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefit outweighs the risk. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable when coadministered with topiramate, and concomitant use may increase menstrual-related adverse effects. 29. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with CYP3A substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose according to product labeling. 30. Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Atazanavir may increase or decrease the levels of norethindrone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 32. Cenobamate decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Increase the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as needed when coadministered with cenobamate. 33. Clobazam decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clobazam is a weak CYP3A4 inducer, and hormonal contraceptive effectiveness may be diminished. Additional nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 34. Colesevelam decreases the levels of norethindrone by drug binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Use caution and monitor closely. Administer oral contraceptives containing norethindrone/ethinyl estradiol at least 4 hours before colesevelam to avoid decreased absorption. 35. Crofelemer increases the levels of norethindrone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Crofelemer has the potential to inhibit CYP3A4 in the gut but is unlikely to inhibit it systemically due to minimal absorption. 36. Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 37. Elagolix decreases the levels of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates if coadministered and consider increasing the dose if needed. 38. Encorafenib both inhibits and induces CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may result in increased toxicity or decreased efficacy. 39. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Adjust the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as necessary. 41. Fosamprenavir has an unspecified interaction mechanism with norethindrone. Use caution and monitor closely. Use nonhormonal contraception. 42. Iloperidone increases the levels of norethindrone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may lead to increased plasma levels of drugs eliminated by CYP3A4. 43. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Norethindrone decreases the effects of insulin degludec by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Progestins may impair glucose tolerance. 45. Norethindrone decreases the effects of insulin degludec/insulin aspart by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Progestins may impair glucose tolerance. 46. Norethindrone decreases the effects of inhaled insulin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Progestins may impair glucose tolerance. 47. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Istradefylline 40 mg/day increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials. This effect was not observed with 20 mg/day. Consider dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 48. Norethindrone decreases the levels or effects of lamotrigine by increasing hepatic clearance. Use caution and monitor closely.
